AgentBlock.description: An agent at work: the client fills in its live state. Exactly one of `taskId` and `threadRef`.

oneOf.description: Markdown, rendered in the app's own style.
A whole HTML page, rendered sandboxed: its scripts run, with no network and no reach into the app.

ArtifactName.description: Lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, at most 64 characters

ArtifactPublished.description: A chat line's artifact: one was published (`artifact_publish`). The app shows it as a card that opens it.

AskBlock.description:
A question for the human, as buttons: Approve and Deny without `options`, one of `options` with them. The
answer is the human's chat reply (`chat_send` with the button's label as its text), so only the human answers
it; an agent's message never does. A command that needs approval still goes through `gated_run`.

AttachmentBlock.description: An image, clip or file already uploaded to the hub: its bytes come from `attachment_get`.

name.description:
The file's name, type and size, filled in by the hub from the file itself when the message is final, so a
client shows its card without reading it; whatever the lead wrote there is replaced.

AttachmentMime.description:
A file's type, as the hub keeps attachments: images, PDF, text and CSV, Office documents and zip archives. The hub
checks a file's bytes against its type ([`AttachmentMime::fits`]) before it keeps it.

AttachmentRef.description: A file on a message: what the app shows without fetching it. Its bytes come from `attachment_get`.

ChartBlock.description: A line, bar or area chart: `x` labels along the bottom, one value per label in each series.

oneOf.description:
An agent or integration writing with its own key (`fleetd chat` with an agent key): input for the lead, never
the human. It approves nothing, answers nothing that is the human's, and leaves needs-you as it was.
fleetd itself: one-line events (a PR merged, an agent started, a past order's state).

ChatBlock.description:
One block: `v`, the block schema's version (`BLOCK_VERSION`), and its kind's fields. A kind or version a client
doesn't know shows as the part's text.

oneOf.description:
A file as a card (its name, type and size) the person opens or saves: one they sent, or one the lead or its
tasks made and uploaded with `chat_file`.

ChatClient.description: Where a human message was written.

oneOf.description: The desktop app.
`fleetd chat`.
The phone's share sheet: what another app shared, with the person's note.

An iOS Shortcuts action (Send Message), run by the person or by one of their automations. Its text may hold
what the shortcut pulled from elsewhere.

ChatDelivery.description: How a human message reached the lead.

oneOf.description: The lead was idle: the message started its next turn.
The lead was mid-turn: it takes the message at its next step, as a steer.
The lead was mid-turn and the human asked for now: its running step stopped for the message.
The lead is starting, or its machine is away: the message waits and goes in as soon as it can.

ChatHistorySource.description:
Where a history message came from, for messages from before the chat existed (a read model; nothing is moved or
destroyed). Absent on messages written in the chat.

oneOf.description: An order's text as it was submitted.
A person's note on an order.
A person's steer to the lead or one of its agents.
What the lead said in its own session.
An order's outcome (done, stopped, failed) as a one-line event.
A question the lead asked with the retired questions tool, and its answer.

ChatItem.description: The two things a chat can't carry as plain text, shown inline in place of the message text.

artifact.description:
A system line "Published …": a lead, task or Navi published an artifact (`artifact_publish`); the app shows a
card that opens it.

by.description: The name of the key that wrote it: a person's device for a human message, the agent for an agent's.

client.description: A human message: where it was written.

clientRequestId.description: A human message: the `clientRequestId` its `chat_send` carried, for the app's optimistic copy.

delivery.description: A human message: how it reached the lead.

history.description: From before the chat: where this history message came from.

memoryRefreshed.description:
A system line "Memory refreshed: +a ~b −c": what the nightly memory refresh changed, each change undone on its
own or all together with `memory_undo`.

nudge.description: The lead flagged it for the person's look (`nudge`).

parts.description:
A final lead message of more than one bubble, or with a block: its bubbles in order. Absent: `text` is one
bubble (and while a message streams).

person.description: A human message: the person who wrote it. Absent from a hub before people.

remembered.description: A system line "Remembered: …" or "Forgot: …": what the lead's `remember` or `forget` wrote, which `memory_undo` takes back.

replyTo.description: A human message: the bubble it answers.

setupChanged.description:
A system line such as "Added the repo api": the lead changed its project's setup, which `project_setup_undo`
takes back.

skillSaved.description:
A system line "Saved a skill: …": a Navi saved or changed one of its skills (`skill_save`); the app links it
to the skill.

skills.description: A human message: the skills it named with `$name`, which the lead's copy lists.

text.description: Markdown. Empty while a streamed message has no text yet, and for an inline `item`.

updatedAt.description: Set when the text was last appended to, or an item's state changed.

vaultImport.description:
A system line with an import card: a lead proposed importing items from 1Password into the vault
(`vault_import_propose`); the person answers with `vault_import`.

worktreesKept.description:
A system line "Cleanup kept 6 worktrees with unsaved work": the worktrees one nightly cleanup kept for work only
they hold.

oneOf.description: The lead is still writing it: `chat_delta` frames append to its text until it is `final`.

ChatNudge.description:
A message worth the person's look: a showcase, something to try, a risk. It waits, below what the lead waits on
you for, until the person has seen the message or dismissed it, and for a day at most. In the app only: it sends
no notification.

cleared.description: Why it no longer waits; absent while it does (or once a day has passed).

reason.description: What to look at, in a few words: "the Machines page redesign".

oneOf.description: The person has seen the message: scrolled into view, or opened with Show.
A newer nudge of its kind took its place past [`CHAT_NUDGES_MAX`].
A day passed unseen.

ChatPart.description:
One bubble of a lead message: `text.slice(start, end)` (UTF-16 offsets, like `ChatDelta.offset`), shown as
markdown, or as `block` when it has one (the slice is then the block's fence, its readable fallback).

ChatReplyTo.description:
The bubble a human message answers: a lead message and the bubble's place in it, as `parts` counts (0 for a
message of one bubble). The lead reads that bubble whole over the reply, and when it was written.

CheckerNote.description: What a Navi's approval checker said of an action it didn't let through.

reason.description: Its reason, in one line. A checker that failed or answered nothing readable says so here.

CheckerVerdict.description: The checker's verdict on a risky action: go runs it, ask brings the person's card, block refuses it.

CommandApprovalItem.description:
A risky command (prod write, spend, delete, credential use), a session's permission prompt, a purchase or a secure
input waits for the human: exactly what it would do, then Approve or Deny. Answered with `approval_answer`, naming
`requestId`. Exactly one of `gated`, `permission`, `purchase` and `secureInput`.

by.description: The key name of the person who answered.

finishedAt.description: Once it ran or failed: when the result came back.

gated.description: A gated command: exactly what runs once approved.

machineId.description: Where it runs, or the machine of the session that asks.

note.description: Why it is open again ("not run: the node was offline when approved"), or why it failed without running.

outputTail.description: The end of the output, once it ran.

permission.description:
A session's permission prompt: the tool and what it would do. Boxed: with its input it is large beside the
item's other fields, and every chat item would carry its size.

purchase.description:
A Navi's purchase (purchase_request): the shop, the total, what it buys and the card. Approved, the Navi's node
fills the card into that checkout once. Boxed, as `permission` is.

secureInput.description: A Navi's secure input from a 1Password field: approved, its node fills that field once.

oneOf.description: Approved and run: see `exitCode` and `outputTail`.
Approved, and the node could not run it.

DiffBlock.description: Changes to show: the files with their hunks, or a PR whose diff the client reads. Exactly one of the two.

hunks.description: Unified-diff hunks, each from its `@@` line.

GatedRunSpec.description: Stored with the approval and never changed: the human approves exactly these bytes.

path.description: Where it is on that machine.

unsaved.description: What only it holds: "uncommitted changes", "2 unpushed commits".

MemoryRefreshed.description:
What a nightly memory refresh changed, as one line in the project's chat: each change with its own Undo, and Undo
all. Posted only when something changed.

items.description: In the order the refresh made them; the first [`REFRESHED_LISTED`] when it made more.

total.description: Every change it made, when that is more than `items` lists. Undo all takes them all back.

undone.description: How many of all its changes are undone, when any is: those past `items` too, which the line doesn't show.

oneOf.description:
The person's own memory: how they work across every project. One shared `user.md` on a hub from before
people.
This project's `MEMORY.md`, or one of its topic files.

NaviCard.description:
The card a Navi pays with: a vault card, or a Credit Card item in its person's 1Password. Only the reference is
kept.

label.description: A vault card's label, brand and last four digits, as the hub reads them: `Visa (Personal)`, `visa`, `4242`.

PersonRef.description:
Who did something, with their name at the time: on chat messages, approvals, secrets, decisions and checklist
changes.

PrBlock.description: A pull request: the client fills in its live state (title, checks, review, merged) from the hub.

title.description: Shown until the live title is known.

ProjectRef.description:
A project: a workspace with a lead and its own directory, on its home machine, where the lead runs. Its
`projectId` is the node's id for that directory, so the ref also addresses the files; the directory may be a git
repo or a plain folder. A project holds zero or more repos (`ProjectRepo`), each in a node directory of its
own or in the project's.

Purchase.description: A purchase as its request keeps it: what the person approves.

card.description: The Navi's card when it asked.

filledAt.description: When its card was filled into the checkout; absent until then. A purchase fills once.

sessionId.description: The browser session that asked, the one its fill is for.

amount.description: Its price in the total's currency, when the checkout shows one.

name.description: What it is, as the checkout names it: `Double room, 12-14 Nov, 2 nights`.

PurchaseShop.description: The shop the lead buys from.

domain.description:
The checkout page's host: `shop.example.com`. The card fills only on it (and its subdomains) and in its
payment provider's frames.

name.description: Its name, as the shop calls itself: `Hotel Adlon`.

PurchaseTotal.description: The total the checkout shows, with everything in it (taxes, fees, shipping).

RememberedItem.description: What a `remember` or `forget` call wrote, as a line in the project's chat. Undone with `memory_undo`.

person.description: User scope: whose memory it is in. Absent for the shared `user.md` of a hub from before people.

replaced.description: The whole entry it replaced, which Undo puts back.

text.description: The entry written; with `forgotten`, the whole entry removed.

SecretFingerprint.description: 8 lowercase hex characters: the sha256 prefix of the plaintext

SecretRequestItem.description:
The lead needs a secret. The app shows a masked field; the value never enters the transcript: it is sealed to the
sink's machine and answered with `secret_submit`, naming `requestId`. Only its fingerprint comes back.

by.description: The key name of the person who answered.

envName.description: An `env:` sink: the variable it writes, when not the one `name` gives (`secrets::secret_env_name`).

note.description: Why it is open again, or why it could not be stored.

secureInput.description: A Navi's secure input (`fill:` sink): the site, the field and why; what is typed fills that field, once.

text.description: One line: why the lead needs it.

SecureInput.description: A secure input as its request keeps it.

filledAt.description: When it was filled; absent until then. A secure input fills once.

sessionId.description: The browser session that asked, the one it fills in.

SecureInputSite.description: The site the field is on.

domain.description: The page's host: `passport.gov.example`. The value fills only on it (and its subdomains).

name.description: Its name, as it calls itself.

SetupChangeKind.description: What a lead's setup call changed. `look` is the icon, picture or color; `env` the plain variables.

SetupChanged.description:
What a lead changed about its project's setup (`repo_add`, `repo_remove`, `project_setup`), as a line in the
project's chat. A person takes it back with `project_setup_undo`.

names.description: The repo it added or removed, or the variables it set or removed.

SkillName.description: Lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, at most 64 characters

SkillSaved.description:
A chat line's skill: a Navi saved or changed one (`skill_save`), or installed one (`skill_install`). The app links
it to the skill's view.

installed.description:
Installed: the source as the Navi gave it, at the commit it is pinned to (`owner/repo@<12 hex>`). `why` then
says the same, for an app that doesn't know this field.

TableBlock.description: Rows of plain-text cells, one per column.

ToolAction.description: What an asking tool would do, for the card's heading and its urgency.

oneOf.description: Reaches another person: an email, a reply, an invitation or an answer to one.
Changes something of the person's: a draft, a label, a page, a document.
Removes something: a message, an event, a page, a file.
Gives someone else access to something.
Pays or buys: money leaves the person's account.
A Navi's final Confirm or Submit click on a site (`confirm_step`): a booking, a cancellation, a form sent.

ToolPermission.description:
An approval raised by a session's tool permission prompt instead of a gated command: answering it answers the prompt
on the project's node. Its machine is the request's project's.

checker.description:
A Navi's approval checker judged it before it reached the person (W239): why it asks them, or why it refused
it. A blocked prompt was already refused on its node; approving it anyway lets the Navi run exactly this input
once, when it asks again.

input.description:
The tool's input exactly as the session asked (at most 64 KiB of JSON): approved, the tool runs with exactly
this. Absent when the node didn't send it; the tool then runs with what the session asked.

preview.description:
An integration's asking tool (`hub/integrations`): exactly who it reaches and what it says, or what it changes,
read from the input it runs with once approved. Boxed: it is large beside the prompt's other fields.

screenshot.description: A Navi's `confirm_step`: its screenshot of the page, the project's, for the card.

site.description:
A Navi's first fetch or browser visit to this site (its host, such as `example.com`): approved, the Navi may
fetch and open it without asking from then on, until a person revokes it (`navi_site_revoke`).

summary.description: The command, the path, or the tool's own description.

ToolPreview.description:
What an approval card shows for an asking tool: what it does and everything it gets. The input is the exact one
the tool runs with once approved; nothing is a summary the agent wrote.

input.description: Everything the tool gets, as JSON.

server.description: The configured server's name, as claude prefixes its tools (`mcp__<server>__<tool>`).

title.description: What it does, as a verb phrase the app puts after "<the Navi> wants to": "Use create_page on docs".

VaultImportCard.description:
A chat message's import card (`ChatMessage.vaultImport`): a lead proposed importing these items; the person ticks
and taps Import (the `vault_import` tool with `proposalId`) or Dismiss. The only confirm in the vault.

imported.description: How many were imported, once answered.

scope.description: Where the items go unless the person picks another: the person's own by default.

VaultImportCardItem.description: One item of an import card.

oneOf.description: An environment variable for agents' sessions.

VaultScope.description: Whose an item is, and so who lists, changes and reveals it, and which work uses it.

oneOf.description: One person's: used by work they started, and projects it's shared with.
One project's (`machineId`, `projectId`): its leads and agents use it.
One order's variable (`workstreamId` too): that order's agents. Gone when the order closes.
Everyone's on the hub, every project's work; only admins change it. Never a variable.

WorktreesKept.description:
The worktrees one nightly cleanup kept in a project because they hold work that exists nowhere else, as one line
that opens to each: what frees it is pushing or deleting that work.
